question: A single intramuscular injection of Vitamin K 1 mg at birth is the recommended prophylaxis for all newborns to prevent VKDB, and it is superior to oral prophylaxis in preventing the late form of VKDB.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. IM Vitamin K 1 mg at birth is the recommended and most effective prophylaxis. It prevents all three forms of VKDB including the late form. Oral prophylaxis requires multiple doses (birth, 1 week, 4–6 weeks) and is less reliable at preventing late VKDB, particularly in infants with subclinical cholestasis who cannot absorb oral fat-soluble vitamins adequately.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! IM Vitamin K 1 mg at birth is the standard of care. IM prophylaxis provides a depot that sustains adequate Vitamin K levels for months — virtually eliminating all three forms, including late VKDB. Oral prophylaxis (3 doses at birth/1 week/4–6 weeks) reduces but does not eliminate late VKDB risk because absorption can be variable and compliance with subsequent doses is unreliable.
